analysis.title: US CPI Lights Up Fed Hike Expectations
key_insights: September core CPI rose 0.33% m/m SA against consensus of 0.2% and Scotia's 0.3%. Total CPI rose 0.65% m/m vs consensus 0.6% and Scotia 0.6%.
Year-over-year rates rose to 3.7% for total CPI (3.4% prior) and 2.6% for core CPI (2.4% prior).
Core goods CPI (ex-food and energy) rose 0.3% m/m SA and is on an accelerating annualized trend. Scotia attributes this to pass through of commodities and tariffs.
Core services CPI (ex-housing and energy services) rose 0.4% m/m SA and annualized rates continue to post sharp increases, with pass through effects also seen here.
Early mapping from CPI points to total PCE tracking +0.45% m/m SA and core PCE tracking +0.27% m/m SA. Scotia will reassess after tomorrow's producer prices.
Scotia says underlying US inflation remains warm and does not rule out another Fed hike on October 28th despite some FOMC official guidance.
Market pricing for the October 28 meeting rose from about 5bps to about half of a 25bps hike after the print.
The jump in core CPI came from seasonally unadjusted prices, which were dampened by another relatively tame seasonal adjustment factor for September.
Breadth of inflationary pressures remains high, though smoothed m/m price increases fall into a lumpy profile.
Energy CPI rose 5.2% m/m and 20.4% y/y. Gasoline rose 9.1% m/m and 34.2% y/y, contributing 0.35 points to the m/m change.
Public transportation CPI is up 15.6% y/y and 1.2% m/m. Motor vehicle insurance is down 5.0% y/y and health insurance down 9.0% y/y.
